title: Acts 19:1–20
context: In Ephesus Paul finds about twelve disciples who know only John’s baptism and have not heard of the Holy Spirit. He explains that John pointed to Jesus; they are baptized in Jesus’ name, and when Paul lays hands on them, the Spirit comes and they speak in tongues and prophesy. Paul preaches in the synagogue for three months, then teaches daily in the hall of Tyrannus for two years, so that all Asia hears the word. God does extraordinary miracles through him. When the seven sons of Sceva try to use Jesus’ name as a formula, an evil spirit overpowers them, and many believers confess their practices and burn their magic books. The word of the Lord grows mightily.

verses.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul finds disciples in Ephesus. Arminian readers see believers whose knowledge is incomplete.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see followers of John who have not yet heard the full gospel.

verses.text: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
verses.arminianNotes: “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They had not heard of the Spirit. Wesleyan and Pentecostal readers often see a subsequent experience implied; other Arminians see incomplete conversion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that these men had not yet believed in Jesus as the Christ, so their case is not a pattern of two-stage Christian experience.

verses.text: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
verses.arminianNotes: They were baptized into John’s baptism. Arminian commentators see the gap explained.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see John’s baptism as preparatory.

verses.text: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
verses.arminianNotes: John’s baptism was repentance pointing to the one coming after him, Jesus. Arminian readers see repentance leading to faith in Christ.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see John pointing beyond himself.

verses.text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.arminianNotes: They are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Arminian expositors see faith expressed in Christian baptism.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors note this is not rebaptism of Christians but the first Christian baptism of John’s followers.

verses.text: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul lays hands on them, the Spirit comes, and they speak in tongues and prophesy. Arminian readers see the Spirit confirming their faith.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see another moment, like Samaria and Caesarea, marking a new group joined to the church.

verses.text: They were about twelve men in all.
verses.arminianNotes: There are about twelve men. Arminian commentators see a small beginning.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see a nucleus for the Ephesian church.

verses.text: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul speaks boldly in the synagogue for three months about the kingdom of God. Arminian readers see persuasion over time.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the kingdom at the heart of his preaching.

verses.text: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
verses.arminianNotes: When some become hardened and speak evil of the Way, he moves to the hall of Tyrannus. Arminian expositors see people hardening themselves through persistent refusal.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see hardening as both human refusal and God’s judicial response.

verses.text: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.arminianNotes: This continues for two years, and all Asia hears the word. Arminian readers see the gospel offered to an entire region.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the word spreading through a central teaching ministry.

verses.text: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,
verses.arminianNotes: God does extraordinary miracles by Paul’s hands. Arminian commentators see God confirming the message.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators note that God is the one working.

verses.text: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
verses.arminianNotes: Even cloths from his body heal the sick. Arminian readers see God meeting people at their level of understanding.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see an unusual measure of power that does not set a pattern for relics.

verses.text: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”
verses.arminianNotes: Itinerant Jewish exorcists try to use the name of Jesus whom Paul preaches. Arminian expositors see people using Jesus’ name without knowing him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the name treated as a magic formula.

verses.text: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
verses.arminianNotes: Seven sons of Sceva, a chief priest, try it. Arminian readers see religious pedigree without faith.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see outward status without inward grace.

verses.text: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”
verses.arminianNotes: The spirit says, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?” Arminian commentators see that only a personal relationship with Christ carries authority.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the powers of darkness recognizing Christ’s true servants.

verses.text: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.arminianNotes: The man overpowers them, and they flee naked and wounded. Arminian readers see the danger of trifling with spiritual power.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God exposing counterfeits.

verses.text: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
verses.arminianNotes: Fear falls on all in Ephesus, and Jesus’ name is magnified. Arminian expositors see reverence growing.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God glorifying his Son.

verses.text: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.
verses.arminianNotes: Many believers come confessing their practices. Arminian readers see repentance continuing after conversion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see sanctification uncovering hidden sins.

verses.text: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
verses.arminianNotes: Practitioners of magic burn books worth fifty thousand pieces of silver. Arminian commentators see costly repentance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the gospel breaking idolatry’s hold.

verses.text: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.
verses.arminianNotes: The word of the Lord grows mightily and prevails. Arminian readers see the gospel advancing against opposition.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the word as the agent of the kingdom.
